- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5), model often overshoots downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid premature correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overreacts with continued steep rise; cap forecast slope at 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model shows mean-reversion bias — forecast should be closer to recent 7-day average, not 30d trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history includes a recent -1.00 (strong bearish signal), model tends to underestimate true drop; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast for next 3–5 days.
